label: OpenCode
description: One conversation with OpenCode, the open source coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, OpenCode runs on your machine (a local install only) with your own login, working in `folder`. If `opencode` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. It must be OpenCode 2: an `opencode` 1 is refused, since it would run with every action allowed whatever the permission setting says. Out of the box OpenCode asks for nothing, so each permission setting is a list of rules weft hands it, which win over the folder's own `opencode.json`. Refusing one of its permission requests ends its whole turn. Claude Code's folder (`~/.claude`), which OpenCode would read as its own config, is kept out. Your program's tools reach OpenCode under their plain names, as tools of the model's own, through a plugin weft writes for it, and a tool named like one of OpenCode's own (`read`, `shell`, `edit`, `subagent`, its `question`, ...) takes that one's place. `execute`, the tool OpenCode runs code with, is refused when the program is built. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission rules, the model, the effort and extra folders.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run OpenCode in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A OpenCodeAccess's `access`: a model provider's key (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Gemini, or OpenCode Zen). Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, OpenCode uses the providers already set up there, and its free models need no login at all.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder OpenCode works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the OpenCode program to run, when it is not the `opencode` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What OpenCode may do without asking. `ask`: commands, edits, web fetches and searches, and folders outside `folder` come out of AskAgent as questions; reading, searching and your program's tools go ahead. `accept_edits`: the same, but edits go ahead. `plan`: its plan agent, which edits nothing but its plan, and asks before the rest. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: The model as `<provider>/<model>`, such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`. Left out, OpenCode's default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Effort
inputs.description: How hard the model thinks, on the models that take it. Left out, the model's default.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` OpenCode may read and change.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: OpenCode '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
OpenCode '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a OpenCodeAccess on `access`.
OpenCode '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
OpenCode '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, accept_edits, plan, bypass.
OpenCode '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
OpenCode '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs OpenCode itself.
